visualReview.notes: Inspected the standing main front, giant six-column order, round-headed entrance arches, steps, corner mansards, central cupola, western stack elevation, rear wing and three light wells. Inspected the final roof and stone finishes after revision.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected four directions, overhead location and four architectural views. The plaster and trim retain relief, glazing stays dark, and the metal roof retains its identifiable profile. Viewer unload passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected the 25 documented medium-fi frames at four detail levels, with both lighting settings, full exterior context and comparison views. Targeted vertical intersection checks confirm that all three native light wells remain open at every level, with an adjacent continuous main roof and covered central cupola.

geographicReview.notes: The named library multipolygon and its three light wells set the outline. The entrance approaches the independently frozen Terrarium field at the mapped Alameda facade. The unmasked field was pictured and inspected separately. The geographic viewer fixture used flat terrain. The city elevation includes terrain and urban return artifacts, and fine rear-contact estimates remain approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: The standing Biblioteca Nacional de Chile and its Alameda facade, with the domed central entrance, two pavilion roofs, long side and rear elevations and three mapped light wells.
fidelityReview.notes: The verified archival image and contemporary footprint support the symmetrical Alameda composition, central arched portico, corner pavilions, dominant dormered cupola and projecting wing mass. The 1924 architectural publication corroborates the retained main and stack elevations. Roof colors, window detail, height, relief and small features are reconstructed estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Started with the Bureau of Public Roads photograph already published by Qualla. Native Commons and NARA identification, public-domain agency release, and exact source bytes were verified. The freely reproducible public-domain 1924 architectural publication is also recorded by catalog item and original PDF hash. The model uses generated surfaces.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Standing library, its six columns and arched Alameda entrance, cupola and mansards, adjoining library wings and three light wells within the named relation.

limitations: The standing library includes the main Alameda pavilion and as-built wings with the mapped light wells. The adjoining separately mapped Archivo Nacional and its original, partially unbuilt proposals remain outside the library geometry.

The contemporary footprint sets the horizontal envelope. Original archive views and published architectural descriptions control the entrance bay, roofs and major facades. Exact facade and roof heights, window frames, roof colors and minor ornament are estimates.
Alameda entrance grade follows the frozen open elevation field. The source also preserves the slope toward Cerro Santa Lucía and urban height artifacts. Rear and courtyard grades are approximate.
